label: fed-back b early in the copy phase (strongest when b is the first original token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is b (the model re-reading its own output b). It never fires on b in the original phase or at the delimiter. It only fires early in the copy phase: recall_idx 1-3 (b was original token 0-2), and absolute step t <= ~9; b fed back later or in long sequences is essentially silent. Magnitude is largest at recall_idx 1, the step right after <DEL> when the first original token is b: this carries 84% of the activation mass, and the top activations (~4.7) are all b as first token in short sequences (L=4-5). Activations get weaker as recall_idx, t and L grow; b at recall_idx 2-3 gives only ~0.2 of max. Most false positives are b at recall_idx 2-3 near t=8-9, where the feature drops to zero.

issues: The factual claims hold up. Activation is entirely in the copy phase (1 active step outside it), entirely on in_tok b (100% of mass), and recall_idx 1/2/3 carry 0.837/0.118/0.046 of the mass, with recall_idx >= 4 essentially silent. The largest mass cells are recall_idx 1 at L=4-6.

The rectangular cutoff (t <= 9 & recall_idx <= 3) is the wrong shape. Precision of copy-phase b by (recall_idx, L) on dev: r=1 is 1.0 for L=3-7, 0.85 at L=8 and 0.13 at L=9. r=2 is 0.97/0.96 at L=4/5, 0.58 at L=6, 0.07 at L=7 and 0.003 at L=8. r=3 is 0.88 at L=4, 0.29 at L=5, 0.03 at L=6 and ~0 after that. The cutoff in L tightens by 2 for every step of recall_idx, so the boundary runs diagonally at L + 2*recall_idx <= 10 (equivalently t + recall_idx <= 10). It is not a fixed t <= 9 box.

So the predicate has a systematic class of false positives: b at r=2 with L=7 (t=9, precision 0.07) and b at r=3 with L=5-6 (t=8-9, precision 0.29 and 0.03). These pass t <= 9 & recall_idx <= 3 but are almost always silent. The explanation mentions these false positives but treats them as leftovers instead of fixing the boundary.

Test scores for the original predicate: precision 0.714, recall 0.984, F1 0.828. The diagonal predicate scores precision 0.912, recall 0.941, F1 0.926 and mass recall 0.991 on test. Its remaining misses are tiny activations (<0.15 of max) right on the boundary, and its false positives sit at boundary cells like r=1 L=8 and r=2 L=6. That is scattered edge noise, not a new pattern.
